text: Thank you, doctor, for your good advice, even though I couldn't follow all your advice. However, the extraction and filling of the tooth by the doctor were very effective. The soreness in my cheeks and gums disappeared. I am very happy. Thank you.

***I think I won't be coming to this dental clinic anymore.
It's not that this place is bad; it's good, many of the doctors are good, and the staff are polite and courteous.
But I encountered one doctor who spoke to me rudely.***

The story is:
In 2023, I came because my tooth was broken.
The staff said the doctor would assess and examine my tooth first,
and then I had to book an appointment.
They said I wouldn't get any treatment yet.

The staff informed me that:
During regular hours, I would have to wait approximately 5-10 months.
(Because there was a backlog from the COVID-19 closure period.)

Outside of regular hours, the appointment would be faster,
but I would still have to wait approximately 3-6 months.
The service fees are as shown in the image.
Outside of regular hours, the price is about 30% higher than the regular hourly rate.

February 22, 2024:
I returned for another check-up on the same broken tooth.
(The tooth that made me wait since the previous year.)
I felt like I had waited too long,
so I went to another clinic to get a filling. The dentist there said it could be filled,
because if I left the broken tooth untreated...
It would increase the risk of root infection, so I had it filled. After the filling, there were no symptoms; no pain, sensitivity, or swelling. I lived my life normally.
Then, six months later,
a different dentist from the dental institute
called to say it was my turn.
I consulted with the dentist on the phone about having already had it filled elsewhere.
The dentist said, "Let me check the X-ray of your root canal first," and then said, "From what I see, the root doesn't seem to be seriously damaged.
If it's filled now, it's fine, and you don't need root canal treatment yet."
So, I didn't come to my appointment.

**Yesterday, February 21, 2024,** the filling fell out.
So today, I came to the dental institute, intending to have root canal treatment.

I met a male dentist.
He told me, "You can't have it done today.
You have to wait in line for another year."
(I understand about the waiting list. If I had an appointment, I would wait because I intended to have treatment at the dental institute anyway.)

The dentist
had me lie on the chair and examined my mouth for 2 minutes.
Then
he said, "Why did you get it filled elsewhere and not wait in line here?"
I told him, "Last year when I came, the dentist didn't fill it for me." "So you have to go get it filled elsewhere. If you leave it, germs can get into the tooth root."

Doctor:
"Let me tell you first, root canal treatment is expensive.
And can you afford it?
Because
most of the people who come for treatment have government employee benefits and can claim them."

I replied to the doctor:
"If I'm planning to get treatment,
I have to be able to pay, doctor.
Root canal treatment already costs over 20,000 baht.
The difference in cost, I can pay extra."

The doctor continued:
"In your case, the gum is starting to cover the tooth cavity. We might have to cut the gum and put in a post. And can you afford to wait in line?
Let me tell you first,
the treatment is expensive.
There are other costs you'll have to pay extra, it might be around 25,000-30,000 baht.
**And can you afford it?"

Me -_-
Reply:
"So, what you're saying is, you want me to go to another clinic, right?"

Doctor:
"I'm not telling you to go elsewhere, I'm asking if you can afford it? It's expensive.
And if you want an x-ray..." "You'll have to pay extra for the x-ray," the doctor said. "But the tooth hasn't been treated yet.
So, what do you want? Do you want the x-ray?"
(I was like -___________-
The doctor kept emphasizing the cost of the treatment, saying it was expensive, and asking if I could afford it.)

So I replied,
"If you're saying that,
I think I won't get root canal treatment here.
I'll probably go to an outside clinic.
I'd rather pay more than here, but have peace of mind."

Then,
the doctor said,
"It's up to you.
I'm not telling you to go elsewhere, I'm just letting you decide."

So I walked out of the examination room, paid the fee,
and left.

Sometimes,
when a doctor says to someone who's genuinely interested in treatment, "Can you afford it?
Do you know how expensive it is?
Can you really afford it?"

It's very disrespectful and insulting.

Why would the doctor think that
people who come for treatment here
don't have the money to pay for it?

Speaking disrespectfully to others
reveals a lot about one's character.
And it seems completely unethical.
I felt really bad when I encountered something like this.

I went for a teeth cleaning (tartar removal).

When I entered the room, the dentist asked what I was there for. I said I was there for tartar removal and to have my teeth checked to see what else needed to be done. Before I could even finish, and before the tartar removal began, the dentist told me to lie down. There was no attempt to examine my mouth or do any further checks. I thought the dentist would examine my teeth during the tartar removal and then give me post-treatment advice.

I understand that dental work can be painful, but the dentist was very harsh and unfriendly. It's like, "Isn't it normal to feel pain and tense up during the procedure?" Then, near the end of the tartar removal, the dentist spoke close to my ear, but I couldn't hear clearly because the instrument was so loud. I only heard "wisdom tooth" and the words "impacted tooth." After the removal was finished, I asked if I had any impacted teeth, and the dentist responded sharply, "I said no!" I felt very uncomfortable, but I still asked if I needed any fillings. The answer was yes, or I could have them extracted. I could tell the dentist lacked compassion and wasn't willing to provide good service.

I don't need overly excellent service, just compassion, professionalism, and ethics from a dentist is enough. Or perhaps it's been so many years that the doctor can't even remember how the professor taught when they were students.

Thank you.
